text:
maya: quick sync — I ran a longprefill stress on magnet24b-int8 and hit a nasty quality cliff exactly at the 4096->4097 token boundary. coherent up to 4096, then sudden token corruption and semantic drift. kv index shows wrap/overwrite around that boundary. logs attached.
sasha: can you paste a minimal repro prompt and the command you used? which GPU/shard did this hit?
maya: repro command: `./run_infer --model magnet24b-int8 --prefill 5500 --seq-pad 0 --warmhead=true --device a100-80g-shard3`
maya: minimal prompt (abbrev): `system: you are a helpful assistant
user: Summarize the following long text... <5k tokens filler>` — behaviour consistent when filler pushes continuity past 4096.
ben: saw something similar earlier on a different model. smells like RoPE scaling mismatch when prefill crosses the internal kv page boundary. int8 only? or fp16 also?
maya: fp16 baseline is clean for same prompt. int8 quant shows the drift. difference log snippet:
```
KV last_index=4095 next_index=0
rotary_scale_factor=0.99927 -> 1.00112
decoded_segment: "...the committee agreed on the terms" -> "...the committe� agre on the termz"
```
ciara: fwiw I landed a small change last week to `rotary_scale` that uses `seq_len / base` for >base windows (base=4096). patch was intended for 16k bringup but maybe the branching math is off. I'll look.
sasha: two immediate dirs: (1) triage quant vs runtime: run fp16 vs int8 with identical seeds across [4095,4096,4097,8191,8192] prefill lengths; (2) capture kv dumps + rotary phase tensors at each layer when we cross the boundary.
ben: add a small unit smoke that primes exact edges (4095,4096,4097) — nightly canary should run this on int8 builds.
maya: will run int8 vs fp16 matrix today and upload csv. also will capture `kv_dump_{layer}_{step}.npy` and `rot_phase_{layer}.txt` for the failing run.
perf-bot: alert: 1766111120: staging cluster observed spike in kv-wrap exceptions for magnet24b-int8 — 24 occurrences in last 10m.
ciara: thanks perf-bot. quick note: my change uses integer division in one spot (`base = 4096; mul = seq_len / base`) — might yield 0 for exact multiples in some languages, which would zero-out scaling. i'll repro locally.
sasha: if that is it we should hotfix: guard against integer truncation and add unit tests for multiples of base.
maya: confirmed locally: when seq_len == 8192 the previous code computed mul=2 but in the int8 codepath it ended up 1 due to truncation in the cast; that misaligned rotations after a wrap. reproducer attached.
ben: good catch. can we also check kv-index wrap code that resets pointers? a concurrent race could overwrite the active buffer when prefill threads flush.
ciara: i'm rolling a revert of the rotary branch to the canary channel and will run the expanded edge tests. will post result in ~30m.
sasha: plan documented: 1) revert rotary branch in canary 2) add unit tests for multiples and off-by-one around base 4096 3) run int8 vs fp16 prefill matrix 4) collect kv/rot artifacts for postmortem 5) add smoke to nightly.
maya: thanks — i'll collate artifacts into the ticket. will add comparison gif of decoded tokens so reviewers can quickly see drift.
ben: :thumbsup:
ciara: revert pushed, canary run started (1766111160). will update.
perf-bot: info: 1766111168: canary run completed — kv-wrap exception count back to baseline.
maya: awesome, thanks all. i'll keep monitoring and open a follow-up if drift reappears on larger quant files.
